abstract: In 16 patients with metastatic testicular cancer and 10 age matched male control subjects growth hormone (GH) responses to growth hormone releasing hormone (GHRH; 1 microgram/kg body weight iv.) and thyrotropin releasing hormone (TRH; 200 micrograms iv.) were measured. Basal GH levels and GH levels following stimulation with GHRH or TRH were significantly increased in cancer patients compared to control subjects. 9 patients with testicular cancer were studied both in the stage of metastatic disease and after they had reached a complete remission. In complete remission GH responses to GHRH tended to decrease but the differences did not reach statistical significance. Our data suggest an alteration of hypothalamic and/or pituitary regulation of GH secretion in patients with metastatic testicular cancer.
abstract_ja: 転移性精巣がん患者16例と年齢を一致させた男性対照10例において、GHRH(1μg/kg体重、静脈内投与)およびTRH(200μg、静脈内投与)に対する成長ホルモン(GH)反応を測定した。基礎GH値と、GHRHまたはTRH刺激後のGH値は、対照群と比べてがん患者で有意に上昇していた。精巣がん9例は転移性疾患の段階と、完全寛解に至った後の両方で検討した。完全寛解時にはGHRHに対するGH反応は低下傾向を示したが、有意差には至らなかった。我々のデータは、転移性精巣がん患者におけるGH分泌の視床下部および/または下垂体による調節の変化を示唆する。
